high.title: VN-Index loses 1,900 point mark, adjustment pressure continues through June?
high.summary: Last week, VN-Index only gained slightly in the first session when retesting the 1,900-point resistance zone, before declining in the remaining 4 sessions under profit-taking pressure. The index ended the week down 0.73% to 1,863.49 points. Average liquidity on HoSE reached only about VND 20,440 billion per session, down nearly 25% from the previous week and the lowest since the beginning of the year excluding holiday weeks. Market developments also show money flow is weakening significantly. Trading volume decreased more than 20% compared to the previous week, reflecting cautious investor sentiment as many stock groups remain in correction or prolonged accumulation phases. Foreign investors continued net selling nearly VND 4,920 billion on HoSE, extending the capital withdrawal streak from the market. This decline in VN-Index below key psychological levels signals potential continued weakness in Vietnamese equities, which could pressure the VND and impact foreign investment flows.

high.title: State Bank of Vietnam has noteworthy new moves
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam and the US Treasury Department issued a Joint Statement on Currency. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment under the IMF Articles of Agreement to avoid manipulating exchange rates or the international monetary system to prevent effective balance of payments adjustment or to gain unfair competitive advantage. They agreed that macroeconomic measures or capital controls are not aimed at exchange rates for competitive purposes; other government investment instruments, such as pension funds and foreign investment seeking risk-adjusted returns and diversification, are not aimed at exchange rates for competitive purposes; foreign exchange market intervention is considered an appropriate tool to address both appreciation and depreciation pressures, aimed at addressing exchange rate volatility and maintaining macroeconomic stability during financial market development. This formal agreement provides framework clarity for VND management and should reduce US pressure on Vietnam regarding currency manipulation allegations, supporting VND stability.

high.title: Big 4 group raises deposit interest rates
high.summary: On June 1, according to BIDV's newly announced online deposit rate schedule, online deposit rates for 6-11 month terms were raised to 6.6%/year, up 1.2% from before. For terms from 12-36 months, rates were uniformly raised to 6.8%/year. The 12-18 month term increased by 0.9%, while 24-36 month terms increased by 0.8%. This is quite a strong adjustment compared to the deposit rate level recently. After raising rates, BIDV has brought its online rate schedule on par with most other banks in the Big 4 group. Currently only Vietcombank maintains a slightly lower rate at 24-month term with 6.3%/year. This aggressive rate increase by BIDV signals funding pressure in the banking system and could indicate tightening liquidity conditions, which typically supports VND stability but may pressure bank margins and lending growth.

medium.title: List of 25 banks just adjusted real estate credit "room"
medium.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam issued a circular to 25 commercial banks about adjusting real estate credit growth calculation to support social housing and industrial parks lending. From January 1-December 31, 2026, credit institutions don't need to count increased outstanding credit for social housing and industrial parks/export processing zones toward real estate credit outstanding when controlling real estate credit growth. This policy relaxation for specific real estate segments supports targeted lending while maintaining overall real estate credit controls.

medium.title: Latest bank notification on fast money transfers from 500 million VND
medium.summary: BIDV announced reinstating smart transaction splitting feature for 24/7 fast transfers from VND 500 million and above. The system automatically splits transfers above this amount into multiple transactions of maximum VND 499,999,999 each. BIDV is the first bank to announce reopening automatic splitting for transfers from VND 500 million. Previously, many banks suspended this automatic splitting feature. This technical adjustment facilitates large-value payments and improves financial system efficiency.

medium.title: Evening June 1, gold prices fall very quickly, silver surprises
medium.summary: By end of June 1, SJC gold bar prices were quoted at VND 155.5-158.5 million per tael, down VND 500,000 per tael from morning. Gold jewelry also declined to VND 155.3-158.4 million per tael. Domestic gold prices fell in line with international markets, where gold traded around $4,500/ounce, down nearly $30/ounce from morning. Surprisingly, silver moved counter to gold and rose 0.59% to $75.84/ounce internationally. The sharp gold price decline reflects global market pressures and could impact Vietnam's gold import dynamics.

medium.title: One decade rise of top 3 private banks and "threat" to Big4 position
medium.summary: Ten years ago, the banking sector's profit race was almost exclusively dominated by Big4 banks. However, large private banks like Techcombank, VPBank and ACB have recorded superior profit growth, gradually narrowing the gap with leaders. From positions only one-third or one-fourth of state-owned banks, many private banks now own profit scales of tens of trillions VND annually. This competitive dynamic in the banking sector could impact credit growth patterns, interest rate competition, and overall financial system stability.
